method: Independent static reverse engineering: dnfile/dncil CIL disassembly and resource extraction, isolated pure JavaScript decoder evaluation, PowerShell control-flow review, Authenticode verification, cleave facts including decoded strings, before/after atomscan, and Forager retrieval with provenance. No sample application or payload executed.

trace: Sets TLS 1.2. Decodes its literal Base64 command as UTF-8 and passes that exact variable to Invoke-Expression.

Decoded code creates System.Net.WebClient, sets a 112-character opaque alphabetic User-Agent, downloads https://gitrm.sbs/apix.ps1 into $script, then immediately passes $script to Invoke-Expression. No payload verification, consent UI or legitimate product purpose is present.
Forager cannot retrieve the current endpoint: DNS reports no such host after retries. This failure does not change what the supplied script is designed to execute.

The retrieved Triage behavioral2 report contains the matching initial URL/User-Agent in the actual request records, a 200 response for apix.ps1, follow-on host/OS/AV reporting to start.php and end.php, GETs of assets/2.zip and assets/7za.exe, and a large POST to screen.php. Its process tree records 7za extraction with a password and a dropped 2.exe launch. These are external historical observations, not additional code statically present in the supplied first stage. A screenshot payload and the final EXE were not independently recovered or identified.
samples.reason: Concealed, automatic execution of unverified remotely supplied code with an opaque client token, corroborated by the historical request/process chain, tips the balance to malicious. A first-stage loader identity is justified; a named final malware family is not.
samples.coverage: Two distinct suspicious observations now fire: execution of the encoded source literal and the decoded HTTP result-to-evaluator transfer. No invented persistence, credential theft, injection or final-family trait was added.
samples.missing_context: Historical response bytes and final payload identity were not recovered. No victim deployment/authorization history was supplied.
samples.marker: PowerShell loader: concealed remote eval; improve HTTP traits

trace: Entry method 0x06000072 (RVA 0x455c) uses a conventional PS2EXE PowerShell host, reads the Sleipnir.ps1 manifest resource and submits it to its runspace. The host includes credential, keyboard and progress UI; their CIL paths implement interactive host support rather than credential theft or keylogging.

The only managed resource is a readable 5710-line WPF performance application. UI handlers invoke tweak/profile dispatchers that capture prior state, back it up, apply settings, verify and log history locally. Startup entries are enumerated to manage StartupApproved settings, not to conceal self-persistence.

Profiles can add Defender exclusions for named game paths/processes, cap Defender scan CPU, terminate selected background applications, alter DNS/services/power settings and disable HVCI/VBS/hypervisor/CPU mitigations. These risky capabilities are real and retained. The sensitive settings are exposed in the application UI; no silent malicious install or remote operator dispatch was found.

The EXE requests requireAdministrator. Bare-script UAC self-elevation is consent-based. The piped re-fetch/IEX branch has an unconfigured REPLACE-WITH placeholder and is gated out; this EXE is already elevated by its manifest.

Driver pages use vendor URLs. Optional NVIDIA/Intel silent installation requires HTTPS, Authenticode Valid with the expected vendor name and a successful restore point before launching. Current configured NVIDIA/Intel endpoints return vendor pages, which fail executable signature checks. Forager recovered those pages; the AMD URL redirected to an AMD Download-Incomplete page and failed recovery with HTTP/2 INTERNAL_ERROR. No substituted dependency was found.

osslsigncode independently confirms an intact Authenticode digest and a valid DigiCert timestamp. The signer CN=Sleipnir Local Publisher is self-signed, so public publisher trust is not established. No appended executable or altered wrapper path was found.
samples.reason: Visible application purpose, user-triggered operations, backups/revert/history and verification of downloaded installers explain the sensitive behavior better than a covert malware interpretation. The accurate suspicious Defender exclusion finding remains.
samples.source_label_explanation: PS2EXE packaging, self-signing, administrator requirements, bypass option text and actual security-reducing tuning are plausible heuristic/riskware triggers. The exact external engine rationale is unavailable.
samples.missing_context: No original distribution chain, consent history or victim deployment evidence. BENIGN is a sighted-quarantine assessment, not a trusted-software certification.
samples.marker: Sleipnir 3.23: UI tuning; retain security-reduction findings

samples.identification: Atom’s Connections 1.7.1.0 encrypted peer messaging application
trace: Main -> Run hosts a local HTTP application at 127.0.0.1/localhost, default port 47800. LoadFiles verifies app.pak SHA-256 db2fd6b4dc620bdddf8cad94e451514066e9cd8181f40ba9a4905159800ccc3c before GZip-decompressing length-prefixed records: index.html 616829 bytes, player.html 5019 bytes, vendor/peerjs.min.js 92865 bytes.

Run creates its own 32-byte random device.key protected by user-scope DPAPI. Handle validates Host and cross-site request metadata; /device-key and /save require POST and X-Atoms:1. SafeTarget restricts saves to app picture/document folders, limits components, rejects traversal/reserved names and checks the full path stays inside the chosen root.

EndOtherCopies queries its own executable basename, excludes its current PID and requires the same configured port before killing another copy. RegisterProtocol installs an atoms: URL handler; MakeDesktopShortcut creates the visible launcher. Neither path creates a logon autorun or remote OS command interpreter.

Independently decoded the string-array rotation/Base64 indirection by evaluating only its isolated decoder and wrappers. Recovered application code implements encrypted storage and ECDH/AES messaging, explicit peer connections/invites, media/calls, export/save UI, version checks and optional plugins. No covert command dispatch or credential harvesting was found.

The bundled PeerJS library matches the npm peerjs@1.5.4 dist/peerjs.min.js bytes exactly (SHA-256 ad5d8870d1e389914f9cba8d35be313c4327c69ee0a221e482e9bf7621136fe5). It uses the public 0.peerjs.com broker over TLS.

Forager recovered the current website, version manifest and plugin catalog. Current Neon Arcade 1.8.0 and Atom Math Lab 1.4.0 archives match advertised SHA-256 values and contain games. Their recursive archive scans have no suspicious/hostile findings. The original app verifies plugin hashes and renders plugin content in allow-scripts iframes without allow-same-origin and with connect-src none; messaging and permissions are mediated by the parent.

The PE is unsigned, with no signature trust inferred from declared Ultra Encode, LLC version metadata. Compressed resources and deliberate JavaScript obfuscation are real; extracted index.html and player.html retain their suspicious obfuscator findings.
samples.reason: The reviewed native boundaries, local key management, bounded saves, user-facing messaging flows and unmodified dependency support likely benign software. Obfuscation alone does not establish abuse.
samples.source_label_explanation: Unsigned custom packaging, compressed high-entropy resources, obfuscated JavaScript, a local server, DPAPI, process termination and registry writes are plausible heuristic triggers. The exact external rationale is unknown.
samples.missing_context: No victim deployment or consent history. Current server/plugin content can differ from the historical application. BENIGN routes to sighted quarantine.
samples.marker: Atom's Connections 1.7.1: bounded local peer-messaging app

trait_changes.rationale: The generic WebClient/download text matcher does not establish a saved artifact and belongs in HTTP client observations. WebClient.Download member text is a managed client operation, rather than an Invoke-WebRequest library fact. WebClient construction belongs in client initialization; User-Agent header mutation belongs in user-agent. Invoke-WebRequest name and parsing-option text belong with HTTP client observations. All six matchers, effective file/platform scopes, criticalities, confidence and exclusions are preserved.
trait_changes.consumer_audit: Exact consumers and local references updated. The former download/ membership is retained explicitly in http-response-acquisition, and the former lib/invoke-webrequest membership in powershell-http-observations. The broad lib/ Python PNG consumer cannot match the moved PowerShell/PE/batch/text atoms. The managed/ screenshot consumer is PE/DLL scoped and cannot count the two moved script-only WebClient atoms. Broad client/ consumers were inspected for context and tested with retained positive and benign fixture coverage.
trait_changes.new_detection: encoded-downloadstring-script-variable-eval is suspicious and requires an encoded, adjacent assignment of DownloadString output into $script followed by Invoke-Expression of that same variable. It rejects different variables, rebinding, member access and prefix collisions. The conventional $script spelling is an explicit limit; no claim of arbitrary-variable data-flow analysis is made. Plaintext is intentionally outside this encoded rule.
trait_changes.losses: No supported finding removed or demoted. After mapping relocated IDs, no original sample or the 11 existing attack/benign fixtures loses any trait. No material detection losses.
trait_changes.selector_scope_note: Destination HTTP client/library selectors now also recognize the relocated, accurate Invoke-WebRequest name/parsing-option observations. Required exploit, endpoint or anti-debug/registry contexts remain unchanged. No new objective fires in the original samples, extracted resources or the 11 existing controls. No consumer was weakened or suppressed to alter a verdict.
trait_changes.budget_review: The 101-rule User-Agent catalog was reviewed for duplicate matchers; no exact duplicate matcher was found. The iOS device-family token list requires no User-Agent or HTTP evidence. Its original comments and geofencing suppressor identify a generic iOS-family compatibility list. Move this observation to the existing os/sysinfo/platform/mobile leaf, preserving its matcher, effective scope, confidence, criticality and exact suppressor reference. This corrects supported-claim placement without removing any observation or raising a budget.

verification.focused_cases: 14 bound-transfer, platform-placement and near-miss cases passed; check.py. Platform baseline matching is verified with test-rules because full scan output can strip unreferenced baseline facts.
verification.existing_fixtures: 11 pre-existing attack and benign samples retain their complete finding maps modulo relocation IDs.
verification.scope_equivalence: Six HTTP moves and the iOS-family platform-name move preserve matchers, scope, severity, confidence and exclusions.
verification.additional_move_equivalence: Original iOS-family atom and moved atom are identical dictionaries; effective platform scope is also identical. Exact geofencing suppressor reference migrated.
verification.final_rescans: All three originals and extracted resource/analysis copies rescanned after the final placement edits. Original finding counts: 23, 188, 102; no original or embedded observation lost after relocation ID mapping.

limitations: Atomscan model v18.18 reports its older v18 feature specification against the v19 extractor. Values are reported as observed.

All originals retain calibrated ML level -1. The malicious PowerShell loader rises only from 0.9927902 to 0.99279225 probability and remains off the detection-level grid, despite two accurate suspicious rules. This is a remaining classifier disagreement.

The engine does not expose the custom managed-resource containers as original archive members. Original scans each have one unit. Resources were manually extracted and scanned before/after; derived decoded.js/strings.json scans are distinguished from actual embedded files in the comparison.

The installed scanner rejects a pre-existing documented 101-rule naming budget when CLEAVE_VALIDATE=1. Baseline and after scans used CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 with the same unmodified model/engine; final validation selects the current-source Cleave binary with the reviewed budget. No rules were weakened to accommodate the installed engine.
Historical Triage process/network records are corroboration, not a substitute for reversing the supplied first-stage code, and do not justify adding downstream behaviors absent from its bytes.
